regions.n: BC Sea to Sky and Fraser Canyon

routes.notes: Logging mainline being chip-sealed in sections; expect gravel, construction and trucks.
routes.desc: The only road to the West Coast Trail village of Bamfield, following logging mainlines along the Sarita River to the open Pacific.
routes.hard: Loose sharp gravel and heavy logging trucks; sections are being chip-sealed so surfaces change year to year.
routes.permits: None. Pachena Bay campground needs a booking in summer.

routes.n: Nitinat and Carmanah mainlines (Lake Cowichan to Carmanah)
routes.notes: Active logging roads; fire-season gate closures, no services past Lake Cowichan.
routes.desc: Island logging roads from Lake Cowichan past Nitinat Lake to the giant Sitka spruce of Carmanah Walbran park.
routes.hard: Rough, potholed mainlines with steep pitches into Carmanah; roads can be gated during fire season.
routes.permits: Check Mosaic/TimberWest road access before going.

routes.n: Head Bay Road (Gold River to Tahsis)
routes.notes: Steep, narrow logging road to the west coast; potholes and loose rock.
routes.desc: A steep logging road over the Island mountains to the fjord village of Tahsis on Nootka Sound.
routes.hard: Steep, narrow grades with loose rock and potholes.

routes.notes: Narrow, steep in places; fuel in Zeballos is limited.
routes.desc: A short, rough gravel spur off Hwy 19 down a narrow canyon to the old gold-mining village of Zeballos.
routes.hard: Narrow canyon road with drop-offs and rockfall.

routes.n: Holberg Road to San Josef Bay
routes.notes: Logging mainline to Cape Scott park; no fuel past Port Hardy.
routes.desc: Logging mainline from Port Hardy to Holberg and the trailhead for San Josef Bay at the north tip of Vancouver Island.
routes.hard: Fast gravel with deep loose patches and trucks.
routes.permits: None; Cape Scott camping needs a BC Parks permit.

routes.notes: Snow until June; logging trucks on weekdays.
routes.desc: The classic Sea to Sky gravel climb from the Pemberton Meadows over Hurley Pass into the Bridge River gold country.
routes.hard: Washboard, potholes and tight switchbacks on the climb out of the Lillooet valley.

links.t: DualSportBC: Hurley River FSR, Terzaghi Dam, Highline
DualSportBC: Quick, cold loop through the Hurley

routes.n: Carpenter Lake Road (Lillooet to Gold Bridge)
routes.notes: Pairs with the Hurley for a loop.
routes.desc: Bridge River canyon road along the turquoise Carpenter Lake reservoir; with the Hurley it makes the Pemberton to Lillooet loop.
routes.hard: Narrow canyon sections with drop-offs and rockfall.

links.t: DualSportBC: Hurley, Carpenter Lake, Seton, Marshall Lake

routes.n: High Line Road (Seton Portage to Bridge River)
routes.notes: Very steep and narrow; ride it up, not down, on a big bike.
routes.desc: A steep, narrow climb over Mission Pass linking Seton Portage with the Carpenter Lake road, one of BC's steepest public roads.
routes.hard: Very steep grades with loose gravel and tight hairpins; not for heavy bikes in the wet.

links.t: DualSportBC: Hurley, Carpenter Lake, Seton, Marshall Lake

routes.n: Duffey Lake Road (Hwy 99, Pemberton to Lillooet)
routes.desc: Paved mountain highway from the coast range to the dry Fraser country, famous with every kind of rider.
routes.hard: 13% grades and hairpins; watch gravel on corners.
routes.permits: Joffre Lakes day pass if you stop to hike.

routes.n: Harrison West and In-SHUCK-ch FSR (Harrison Mills to Mount Currie)
routes.desc: Long logging roads up the west side of Harrison Lake and along the Lillooet River, the backroad from the Fraser Valley to Pemberton.
hi: Church of the Holy Cross at Skatin
routes.hard: Potholes, washouts after storms and narrow lakeside sections.
routes.water: Creeks can run over the road in spring melt.
routes.permits: None; Sts'ailes and In-SHUCK-ch nation lands, ride slow through villages.

camps.n: Ten Mile Bay South Group Site
Ten Mile Bay North Group Site

routes.notes: Check the Lytton ferry status before going.
routes.desc: Narrow gravel above the west bank of the Fraser River, ending at the free Lytton reaction ferry.
routes.hard: Narrow shelf road with drop-offs; dusty and very hot in summer.
ferries: Lytton reaction ferry (free, small, check it is running)

routes.notes: Slick when wet; cattle on the road.
routes.desc: Gravel over Pavilion Mountain through ranch land and grassland to Kelly Lake and Clinton, a dirt alternative to Hwy 99 and 97.
routes.hard: Steep, loose climb up Pavilion Mountain; slick clay when wet.
routes.permits: Ranch land: close the gates and watch for cattle.

routes.n: Dog Creek Road (Williams Lake to Clinton)
routes.desc: Ranch-country gravel along the Fraser River grasslands through Alkali Lake, Dog Creek and Jesmond.
routes.hard: Clay surface turns slick when wet.

routes.n: Farwell Canyon and Big Creek loop
routes.desc: Chilcotin grassland loop down into the hoodoos and sand dunes of Farwell Canyon and out through Big Creek.
routes.hard: Steep, loose descent to the Chilcotin River bridge.

routes.n: Nemiah Valley Road (Hwy 20 to Konni Lake)
routes.notes: Dead end; carry fuel for the return.
routes.desc: Remote Chilcotin gravel to the Xeni Gwet'in Nemiah Valley under the Coast Mountains, with wild horses and huge lakes.
routes.hard: Rough, rocky sections and dust; a long dead end with no services.
routes.water: Small creek crossings possible after rain.
routes.permits: Xeni Gwet'in land: respect the community, ask before camping.

routes.n: Freedom Highway (Hwy 20, Williams Lake to Bella Coola)
routes.notes: Make it a loop with the ferry to Vancouver Island.
routes.desc: Across the Chilcotin Plateau to the coast, finishing with "The Hill", a gravel descent of 1,500 m into the Bella Coola valley.
routes.hard: The Hill: 18% gravel grades and hairpins with no guardrails.
ferries: BC Ferries Bella Coola to Port Hardy (summer, book ahead)

stops.n: Tsideldel Gas Station and General Stores

links.t: CDN BKR: Bella Coola 3G
CDN BKR: The over the hill gang, Bella Coola

routes.desc: Cariboo forest gravel linking two gold-rush villages past Quesnel Lake country.
routes.hard: Washboard and logging trucks.

routes.notes: Signage is poor, carry a map.
routes.desc: Gold-rush logging roads past Keithley Creek and Cariboo Lake to the heritage town of Barkerville.
routes.hard: Rough, poorly signed logging roads in the middle.

routes.desc: Gravel across the grasslands of Canada's largest working cattle ranch, Douglas Lake Ranch.
routes.hard: Washboard and cattle guards; slick when wet.
routes.permits: Private ranch roads in places: stay on the public road.

routes.notes: Good link from the Similkameen to the Okanagan.
routes.desc: Gravel through lake country from the Similkameen to the Okanagan, past Osprey Lake and the Kettle Valley Rail Trail.
routes.hard: Washboard; cattle on the road.

routes.desc: Old coal and gold towns on the Tulameen River, then gravel north to Brookmere and Merritt.
routes.hard: Dusty, loose gravel in August.

camps.n: Free camping area along Coldwater River

routes.n: Hwy 31 Lardeau and Trout Lake (Kaslo to Revelstoke)
routes.desc: The quiet gravel side of the Kootenays, along the Lardeau River to Trout Lake and the free Upper Arrow Lake ferry.
routes.hard: Narrow gravel along Trout Lake with potholes.
ferries: Upper Arrow Lake ferry Galena Bay to Shelter Bay (free)

routes.desc: Paved Kootenay classic with two free lake ferries, the Kaslo to New Denver road and the Nakusp hot springs.
routes.hard: Tight paved corners; deer.
ferries: Kootenay Lake ferry Kootenay Bay to Balfour (free)
Upper Arrow Lake ferry Galena Bay to Shelter Bay (free)

stops.n: Creston Tempo Gas Bar & Wand Wash

routes.n: Gray Creek Pass (Gray Creek to Kimberley)
routes.notes: Usually open only July to September; check with the Gray Creek Store.
routes.desc: One of the highest roads in BC, over the Purcell Mountains from Kootenay Lake to Kimberley at about 2,050 m.
routes.hard: Steep, rocky climb and descent with loose sections near the summit.
routes.water: Creek run-off on the road in early summer.

routes.n: Whiteswan Lake and Lussier Hot Springs
routes.notes: Trucks use the road; radio-assisted in places.
routes.desc: Gravel up the White River valley to the free Lussier natural hot springs and Whiteswan Lake park.
routes.hard: Narrow canyon section with logging trucks.

routes.desc: Logging road deep into the Purcells to the granite spires of the Bugaboos and the famous heli-ski lodge.
routes.hard: Rough, rocky last section; porcupines chew parked bikes and cars (bring chicken wire).

routes.n: Elk River FSR to Elk Lakes park
routes.desc: Up the Elk Valley past Elkford to the remote Elk Lakes park on the Alberta border.
routes.hard: Rough, potholed gravel; mining trucks near Elkford.

routes.n: Flathead FSR (Morrissey to the Flathead Valley)
routes.notes: Dead end near the closed Montana border; no services.
routes.desc: Into the wild Flathead Valley, one of North America's densest grizzly areas, next to Glacier National Park.
hi: Glacier park peaks across the border
routes.hard: Rough gravel with washouts in the upper valley.
routes.water: Creek crossings possible on side roads.
routes.permits: None; the border crossing is closed.

routes.desc: The wild route north to the Yukon through the Coast and Cassiar mountains, with bears on the road and few towns.
routes.hard: Patches of gravel and no shoulders; long stretches without services.

stops.n: Dease River First Nation Store & Fuel

camps.n: Dease Lake Lions Tanzilla River Campground
Dease River Crossing Campground and Cabins

links.t: Motorcycle Mojo: Because B.C.
RevZilla Common Tread: The road to Alaska

routes.n: Stewart, Hyder and Salmon Glacier road
routes.notes: Snow at the summit into July.
routes.desc: Past Bear Glacier to Stewart, through Hyder, Alaska, and up a mining road to look down on the Salmon Glacier.
routes.hard: Rough mining road past Hyder with narrow shelf sections.
routes.permits: Passport: no US check entering Hyder, Canada customs on return.

routes.notes: No fuel at the far end some years.
routes.desc: A spectacular gravel road along a lava ridge high above the Grand Canyon of the Stikine to the historic village of Telegraph Creek.
routes.hard: 20% gravel grades on a narrow ridge with drop-offs.
routes.permits: Tahltan territory; the area was burned in 2018, ask in Dease Lake about conditions.

links.t: ExploreNorth: Telegraph Creek Road
Motorcycle Mojo: Because B.C.

routes.n: Omineca gold road (Fort St. James to Germansen Landing)
routes.notes: Carry fuel; services are very limited.
routes.desc: Long gravel into the old Omineca gold fields to Manson Creek and Germansen Landing, deep in the northern bush.
routes.hard: Long rough stretches with mud after rain; very remote.

routes.notes: Paved; long gaps between stations in the north.
routes.desc: The legendary paved road north, through the Rockies at Muncho Lake and past Liard hot springs into the Yukon.
routes.hard: Frost heaves, construction gravel and bison on the road.

stops.n: Datlu Dena Fuels and Convenience Store

routes.n: Forestry Trunk Road South (Coleman to Highwood)
routes.notes: 99 km of gravel with no fuel.
routes.desc: The southern Forestry Trunk Road through the Livingstone Range and Oldman River country, all gravel and big skies.
routes.hard: Strong crosswinds and loose gravel on corners.
routes.permits: Public Lands Camping Pass for random camping.

links.t: CDN BKR: Following the Forestry Trunk Road

routes.n: Forestry Trunk Road (Ghost and Waiparous to Hwy 579)
routes.desc: The busy Ghost and Waiparous section of the trunk road north of Calgary, gateway to the Ghost recreation area.

routes.permits: Public Lands Camping Pass; OHV trails have their own rules.

camps.n: Girl Guides of Canada Camp Mockingbird

links.t: Steve Schwarz: Forestry Trunk Road, Hinton to Ghost Valley (4x4)

routes.n: Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734, Sundre to Nordegg)
routes.desc: The longest classic section of the trunk road, through the Clearwater and Ram river country to Nordegg.
routes.hard: Long gravel with loose corners and dust.
routes.permits: Public Lands Camping Pass for random camping.

links.t: CDN BKR: Following the Forestry Trunk Road
CDN BKR: Alberta backcountry ride
Horizons Unlimited: Hwy 734 Forestry Trunk Road

routes.n: Cardinal Divide and Grave Flats Road (Cadomin to Hwy 734)

routes.hard: Steep, loose climb to the divide; mine trucks near Cadomin.

routes.n: Forestry Trunk Road North (Hwy 40 to Hwy 43)
routes.notes: No fuel for the whole section.
routes.desc: The remote northern trunk road through foothills forest from Grande Cache country to the Peace region.
routes.hard: Fast industrial trucks and dust.

routes.n: Smith-Dorrien Spray Trail (Canmore to Kananaskis Lakes)
routes.desc: Gravel through Kananaskis Country past Spray Lakes and big peaks, from Canmore to the Kananaskis Lakes.
routes.hard: Washboard and heavy traffic; dust.

routes.desc: Canada's highest paved pass at 2,206 m, through the heart of Kananaskis.
routes.hard: Paved; bighorn sheep and bears on the road.

routes.desc: One of the world's great paved rides, along the Continental Divide past glaciers and turquoise lakes.
routes.hard: Paved; traffic stopping for wildlife.

routes.n: Ya Ha Tinda road (Sundre to the Red Deer River)
routes.desc: Gravel up the Red Deer River to the Parks Canada horse ranch on the edge of Banff park, elk country.
routes.hard: Loose gravel and dust.

routes.n: Cypress Hills Gap Road (Elkwater to Fort Walsh)
routes.desc: The dirt road across the Cypress Hills interprovincial park, the highest land between the Rockies and Labrador.

routes.notes: Very hot in summer; carry water.
routes.desc: Gravel through native prairie and the Frenchman River valley, with bison and prairie dog towns.

routes.permits: Some sites are on private land: take the Coronach tour for the caves.

routes.notes: No fuel or services past La Loche.
routes.desc: The far north road of Saskatchewan, through boreal forest and burns toward the Athabasca sand country.
routes.hard: Deep sand and loose gravel.

routes.desc: Up the Churchill River canoe country to Reindeer Lake at Southend.
routes.hard: Gravel north of Missinipe.

routes.notes: Carry fuel and a satellite messenger.
routes.desc: The end of the all-weather road in northern Saskatchewan, a mine-supply gravel road to Points North.
routes.hard: Long rough gravel with mine trucks; very remote.

routes.desc: Gravel over the Manitoba escarpment through Duck Mountain park past Wellman and Childs lakes.
hi: Baldy Mountain, highest point in Manitoba
routes.hard: Loose gravel on hills.

routes.n: Nopiming PR 314 (Lac du Bonnet to Bissett)
routes.desc: Canadian Shield gravel through Nopiming park, granite and lakes everywhere, to the gold town of Bissett.
routes.hard: Narrow, dusty gravel with blind crests.

routes.desc: Long boreal road to the northern mining towns of Leaf Rapids and Lynn Lake.
routes.hard: Gravel sections with potholes.

routes.notes: Fuel only at Split Lake and Gillam.
routes.desc: Remote gravel toward Hudson Bay through Split Lake to the Nelson River dams at Gillam.
routes.hard: Rough gravel with deep potholes after rain.

routes.n: Lake Superior Circle (Hwy 17, Sault Ste. Marie to Thunder Bay)
routes.desc: The paved north shore of Lake Superior, cliffs, beaches and long stretches of wilderness.

routes.permits: Ontario Parks day pass to stop in Lake Superior park.

routes.hard: Fast trucks and dust.

routes.desc: Gravel into old-growth pine country to the landing on Lake Temagami.

routes.desc: Twisty paved Ottawa Valley backroads through the Madawaska Highlands, a classic Ontario sport-touring loop.
